extracted.intended_audience: general news readers interested in health/science reporting
extracted.subtask_description: A news report about a journal retracting a controversial scientific paper, describing the investigation, alleged misconduct, and standards for evaluating the research and retraction process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author permission for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal said it had received permission from everyone named on the May 19, 2005, research paper to make the unusual move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science secured consent from all listed authors before retracting the paper — a procedural safeguard noted by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction wording must reflect final investigation conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: “To ensure that the wording of the retraction reflects the final conclusions of the Seoul National University (SNU) investigation, Science will finalize the retraction text and proceed with the final steps of the retraction process only after the SNU investigation is completed next week.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal delays finalizing retraction language until institutional findings are complete so the notice accurately conveys the investigation's conclusions and as much information as possible to the scientific community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and provision of checkable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “Scientific papers are meant to be written in such a way that other researchers can try to repeat the findings themselves, and are supposed to supply evidence that can be checked.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should include sufficient methods and data so independent researchers can replicate results and verify claims; lack of such information undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review and expert scrutiny prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: “Science is one of the leading peer-reviewed journals and prides itself on subjecting research papers to scrutiny by other experts in the relevant fields. A retraction is rare because usually research is carefully checked before publication.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust peer review and expert oversight are expected to detect problems before publication; retractions indicate failures in that pre-publication scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data authenticity and absence of fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hwang team has been accused of outright fabrications and ethical missteps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be supported by authentic, verifiable data; allegations of fabrication are grounds for investigation and retraction. The article notes DNA tests as a method to reveal whether stem-cell batches are cloned from a person or originate elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent external verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Other stem cell experts have recommended having a lab outside Seoul National University do the testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent testing by external laboratories is recommended to confirm results and avoid institutional bias or errors in verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and informed consent for biological materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleagues accused Hwang of coercing female subordinates into donating their eggs for experiments; there are accusations of ethical missteps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research involving human biological material requires ethical conduct and voluntary, informed consent from donors; coercion or improper recruitment is a serious ethical violation affecting the work's validity and acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of institutional investigation and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Science will finalize the retraction text after the SNU investigation is completed; Science hopes this approach will yield a retraction that will convey accurately as much information as possible to the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and journals should be transparent about investigative findings and communicate clearly to the scientific community when correcting the record, using accurate, informative retraction notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of high-profile endorsements and author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Hwang’s work won credence because of the backing of the journal and it gained further weight when a leading U.S. stem cell expert, Dr. Gerald Schatten, lent his name to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsements or co-authorship by respected experts can increase perceived credibility of research; co-authors and endorsers share responsibility to ensure the work's integrity and can influence how errors or misconduct are received by the community.
